newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weak as NY fund buyers sidelined.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weak as NY fund buyers sidelined.

text.p: White sugar futures edged lower as more fund buying failed to materialise in the raws but volume was light as players were reluctant to sell too aggressively, traders said on Monday.
London players were still nervous to see how the dust settled in New York after heavy fund buying in October sparked a sharp rally in Friday's session, they said.
"It's brought out a few people following New York but the volume is still dead," said one.
"Things are coming in bits and pieces but nobody is wishing to push it down too much," he said.

October raws surged 38 points to hit 11.93 cents/lb on Friday but then slipped to close at 11.86. Concerted buying of March calls at 12.50 cents/lb forced extra position covering and added to the rally, traders said.
At 1455 GMT October whites was down $1.80 at $326.80, just 30 cents off its intraday low. December was 90 cents down at $324.50 and volume reached a light 557 lots.
Broker and commision house players were cited on the sell side but interest was subdued, traders said.

The Paris market was firmer on the day but also slipped after the New York open. October was up $3.00 at $326.50 after hitting a high of $328.00. December was up $4.20 at $325.00 in an overall volume of just 55 lots.
Fundamentally, Syria has tendered to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 of raws for October delivery, as an amendment to the August 7 tender.
